claim: Prompted intrinsic self-critique, with no external signal, does not improve and often lowers LLM reasoning accuracy (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1 after 3 calls; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after 5 calls). UPDATE (gap search): holds for older chat models and low-verifiability tasks; for 2025-26 models and rule-checkable tasks intrinsic self-correction gives gains (Stav 2026: SAT removes 65.66% of errors, Spearman 0.65 with verifiability); reasoning-trained models show no blind spot (Tsui 2026).
agent_test: Run plain answer vs one self-critique round at equal tokens on a held-out set; count right-to-wrong vs wrong-to-right flips.

claim: Earlier self-correction gains came from oracle labels deciding when to stop; with the oracle, GPT-4 HotpotQA rises 49 to 59 and GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5.
agent_test: Allow revision only when a code check or retrieval result changes; compare with an oracle-stop upper bound.

claim: Self-correction works when feedback comes from a reliable external tool (code, search, tests); CRITIC with tools beats the same loop without tools by about 4 to 8 EM points.
agent_test: Same revision loop with and without a tool result at equal tokens.

claim: The weak step in LLM self-audit is locating the error, not fixing it: GPT-4 finds the mistake step 52.87 percent of the time; backtracking at the true location gives +43.92 on wrong arithmetic traces (but -6.67 on right ones).
agent_test: Compare model-chosen vs code-chosen failing step on traces with a known first error.

claim: Multi-agent debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or a strong single-agent prompt at equal compute (GSM8K majority vote 88.2 at 9 responses vs debate about 83). UPDATE: Choi 2025 (voting 0.7691 vs best MAD 0.7377 average, Qwen2.5-7B) and Ferreira 2026 (debate ties or loses at matched budget, 1.6x time, 3.4x tokens) agree; a noise placebo matches self-correction (Bertalanic 2026).
agent_test: Debate vs majority vote vs strong single prompt at matched tokens; adopt debate only if it wins.

claim: Debate gains in the original papers (Du, Liang) shrink or vanish against stronger baselines (Zhang 2025: Society of Mind below CoT on 9 of 9 sets for GPT-4o-mini), yet Du/Liang gains were real against their own baselines.
agent_test: Re-run the Liang counter-intuitive set with CoT plus self-consistency at equal tokens.

claim: Debate can lower accuracy over rounds because agents flip correct answers to incorrect to agree with peers; a weak agent can drag strong ones down.
agent_test: Log flips per round; require every revision to cite new evidence.

claim: Assistants cave when challenged: Claude 1.3 wrongly admitted mistakes on 98 percent of 'are you sure' cases (GPT-4: 42); 'are you sure' cut accuracy up to 27 percent (Claude 1.3); a user-suggested wrong answer cut it up to 27 percent (LLaMA 2). UPDATE: wording matters little (plain repetition 15.0% vs fallacy 12.9%, emotion 13.2%; Yang 2026), 84% of concessions follow the first push, but who flips depends on wording class (Huang 2026).
agent_test: Measure answer flips under neutral vs leading challenge wording.

claim: A model judging its own output prefers it, and the bias grows with self-recognition; same-model challengers share the blind spot.
agent_test: Challenger from a different model family vs the same model at equal tokens.

claim: Role-played devil's advocacy is weaker than authentic dissent and can strengthen the original view (human studies; numbers not read by us).
agent_test: Compare an assigned-opposite persona with a challenger given independent evidence.

claim: Assigned dissent (devil's advocacy, dialectical inquiry) beat consensus or expert-only approaches in lab studies, but consensus groups were more satisfied (numbers unverified).
agent_test: Test quality only; satisfaction does not apply to a solo agent.

claim: Mixing different model families in a debate helps more than same-model copies, though a weak model can hurt. UPDATE: cross-family helps as extra independent votes (heterogeneous c 0.85 to 0.54; roster vote beats best single) but mixed-model debate loses to its own roster vote by 1.04 pp [-1.61,-0.52] (Ferreira 2026); helps keep dissent alive on no-truth policy tasks (Sela 2026).
agent_test: Cross-family challenger vs same-family at equal tokens.

claim: Anticipatory reflection (a pre-mortem inside an agent) gives a small gain on WebArena: 23.5 vs 22.7 (LATS) vs 19.8 (Plan+Act), and 45 percent fewer plan revisions. UPDATE: InvThink premortem cut harm up to 32% vs zero-shot, 16% vs safety prompt, but this is safety, not planning accuracy.
agent_test: Pre-mortem step on planning tasks, gated by a high-stakes signal, at equal tokens.

claim: Structured self-critique can help on well-structured planning without a verifier (Blocksworld 49.8 to 89.3 for Gemini 1.5 Pro) but not for every model (Gemma-2 27B no gain); this limits claim K01 to unstructured tasks.
agent_test: Replicate on our planner with and without critique at equal tokens.

claim: Verification questions answered independently (factored Chain-of-Verification) beat joint verification: FACTSCORE 63.7 vs 60.8, with revise 71.4.
agent_test: Independent checks of each claim vs one joint critique.

claim: Two-sided adversarial debate helps a weak judge when debaters see a source text: judges 76 percent (models) and 88 percent (humans) vs naive 48 and 60.
agent_test: Applies only with an evidence-holding debater; test on a source-grounded question set.

claim: Debate disagreement intensity is a large moderator: higher agreement helped knowledge questions (about +15 percent for Multi-Persona on a 376-question USMLE subset); lower helped a counter-intuitive reasoning set.
agent_test: Vary challenger aggressiveness by task type.

claim: LLM wargame simulations differ from experts: LLMs more aggressive, scenario-sensitive, dialogue farcically harmonious, personas do not change outcomes; all five tested LLMs escalate.
agent_test: An adversary persona must be constrained by scenario facts and checked.

claim: Structured analytic techniques, including alternative analysis, were mandated in 2004 without controlled accuracy tests; one-directional bias warnings may cause the mirror bias; SATs can add noise.
agent_test: Treat military red-team tools as unvalidated; test each on our agent.

claim: Military red-team outcomes have no published accuracy metric; the only numbers (TSA 67 of 70 breaches) are physical penetration tests.
agent_test: Do not import effect sizes from military practice.

claim: Team B (1976) is a cautionary case: predicted about 500 Backfire bombers vs 235 actual; contested whether it was right on core intent.
agent_test: A challenger with no grader can overstate; require a graded outcome.

claim: The Agranat Commission (1973) blamed a fixed 'concept' kept despite contrary warnings; supports attacking the assumption, not only the conclusion.
agent_test: Assumption-listing step: name key assumption, search for disconfirming evidence.

claim: Role definitions differ: CIA devil's advocacy (one dominant view), Team A/B (two competing views), red team analysis (adversary modelling); UFMCS usage is broader and its handbook was not read.
agent_test: Implement separate operators, not one.

claim: Prospective hindsight (pre-mortem) raised correct reasons by about 30 percent in Mitchell et al. (1989); recalled, not re-read.
agent_test: Pre-mortem prompt vs plain forecast; count valid failure reasons.

claim: Consider-the-opposite and dialectical bootstrapping give modest human gains; replication evidence is smaller or conditional (not read).
agent_test: Second estimate after 'assume first wrong', averaged; compare with plain resampling.

claim: Multi-agent LLM systems fail often (41 to 86.7 percent across seven frameworks).
agent_test: Budget for failure; add checks.

claim: An LLM devil's advocate in human groups raised satisfaction but not psychological safety (N=48); a GPT-4o facilitator raised information sharing but not decisions (N=1,475).
agent_test: Human-facing; low relevance to a solo agent.

claim: LM red-teaming (Perez): zero-shot found 3.7 percent offensive replies; RL over 40 percent but narrow (78 percent contained 'invisible'); human red teaming shows RLHF models harder to attack with scale.
agent_test: Attack generators need diversity terms and an external grader.

claim: Self-correction blind spot: models correct an identical error when it is attributed to a user but not when attributed to themselves (64.5% average blind spot over 14 open non-reasoning models); reasoning-trained models show about none; appending Wait cuts the blind spot 89.3% (accuracy e.g. Qwen3-32B 0.045 to 0.793).
agent_test: Present the draft as another agent's output in the audit slot versus own-output framing, and append a Wait step; compare flips at equal tokens.

claim: A random-noise revision prompt matches self-correction and peer content adds nothing in homogeneous teams (GSM-Hard c 0.33 vs 0.34); only architectural diversity lowers the correlation ceiling (c 0.85 to 0.54).
agent_test: Add a noise-placebo arm to every challenge test.

claim: Value of any verifier or critic is bounded by the oracle gap then signal fidelity: public tests +8.14 pp, generated tests +2.70 pp with near-zero harm vs an LLM selector at 4.69% harm; on GPQA-Diamond recoverable mass is 3.03%.
agent_test: Estimate the oracle gap on our tasks before enabling a challenger.

claim: Debate nearly all benefit comes in the first exchange (84.6% at one round, 87.2 at two, flat to five) and mixed teams fix 63.7% of wrong round-one majorities vs 42.9% homogeneous.
agent_test: Cap challenge at one round.

claim: Debate is a martingale in expected belief (Choi 2025); only a bias toward correction helps (MAD average 0.7332 vanilla vs oracle 0.8236 at T=2).
agent_test: Only let the challenge change an answer when new evidence appears.

claim: Human red-team handbook content (UFMCS tool list, ADSO) and the Schwenk and Nemeth numbers could not be opened; still unverified.
agent_test: Obtain the PDFs by other means and extract numbers.
